sources.note: Both shapes claudecode can report. system/subtype:"api_error" -> apiErrorFromSystemEvent reads error.status, retryAttempt, maxRetries, retryInMs and sets Phase=retrying when Attempt or RetryIn is present. An assistant message with isApiErrorMessage:true -> terminalAPIError sets Phase=terminal. The gate is on the boolean VALUE, never on field presence — four recorded ESC interrupts carry isApiErrorMessage:false.
The session_error rule routes a standing SessionError to StateError, and classifyAgentDone routes a hook-delivered turn_done on a FAILED turn to StateError rather than ready.

The parameterised Anthropic stub these three cells drive. --status/--error-type choose the failure, --succeed-after chooses whether it ever clears. Same streamHappyPath bytes as mock-anthropic-429 so a healthy turn is identical across mocks.

The recipe runtime block (bare_mode/env/mock) these cells use instead of a bespoke recorder. run-cell.sh refuses the cell outright if the driver does not declare DRIVE_SUPPORTS for what the recipe asks, and after the drive asserts both the driver's env receipt and that the mock actually served requests.

ErrorPhaseTerminal: 'Only the next turn the user starts clears it.' The clearing predicate is SessionError.ClearedByTurnBoundary, shared by the transcript and hook arms so the two channels cannot disagree.

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full; driver_capability: ready

## Reasoning

The pair to 2.22, differing in ONE mock flag (`--succeed-after 0`). It is the cell that makes the retry-vs-give-up distinction testable: both sessions sit in `error`, and what separates them is whether another attempt is coming and what the session settles to.

Two things must hold that a single failure cannot show:

1. The failed turn's OWN epilogue must not clear the error. `ErrorPhaseTerminal`'s doc says only the next turn the USER starts clears it, and #1799 found the code did not implement that — the session went red and green inside one read pass.
2. The session must not stick in `working` either. Both silent-green and stuck-working are the outcomes #1796 exists to remove.

**No `--retry-after`.** An earlier cut passed `--retry-after 1` to compress the ladder, on the assumption that an unpinned backoff would make the recording minutes long. Both halves were measured false: claude short-circuits a repeated 529 after four attempts in ~2.2s with or without it, and 2-24 measured that claude-code 2.1.245 IGNORES the header entirely (a 401 climbed its own 1,3,5,7,9,10,17,34s ladder while the mock was sending `retry-after: 1`). Leaving it on would have contaminated the one cell that reports a dwell as claude's own behaviour with a flag that does nothing.
